v1.24.0 is the release where a graph holds books and reports it did not make. A ledger kept in
another system can be mirrored into a graph read-only, corrected by the system that keeps it, and
closed in shadow; a fund can load a report from a company that is not on the platform, from a
holon, a Tavi model, or rows read out of a PDF or a workbook. Around that, the SEC repository
opens with a free trial that needs no card, the RoboLedger MCP route shows every operation as its
own tool, and amounts no longer stop at 32 bits.

Covers everything since v1.23.0; the 1.23.x patches carried generated changelogs.

## Books kept in another system

**An external ledger keeps an entity's books read-only.** An `external` connection registered with
`ledger: true` is the keeper of one entity's books, the group parent's by default, under the
`shadow` write policy, the only one it can hold. That ledger's `journal_entry_recorded` events
land posted; a posted entry from any other source, or by hand, is refused, and a draft is
accepted and never posts. An opening balance is allowed as the mirror's starting point. The
close moves the closed-through date, stamps the statements, posts nothing and records its gates
as findings. Registration answers 409 when another ledger keeps the entity's books, the entity
has books of its own, or it is the consolidation entity, and `propose-consolidation-entries` is
refused when every member of the group is mirrored. One source keeps one entity's books. Until
now only a QuickBooks connection could hold that posture, and only for the group parent.

**The ledger that keeps the books corrects what it sent.** `create-event-block` takes
`source_version`, a number the source only increases: the same `(source, external_id)` with a
higher version supersedes the entries the event posted and posts the new ones, and an equal or
lower version is still the 409 of a repeat delivery. `update-event-block` takes
`source_retracted` with `transition_to: voided` to withdraw one. Both apply only to the ledger
that keeps the entity's books, and a correction dated in a closed period is refused by the
existing gate.

**An external source reports its own sync.**
`POST /v1/graphs/{graph_id}/connections/{connection_id}/sync-report` records a run as succeeded
or failed, so a close of mirrored books reads a real `last_sync` in place of a never-synced
finding.

**An event is found by the id its source sent it under.** The `eventBlocks` GraphQL read takes
`externalId`; with `source` it names at most one event. An integration that keeps no state
between runs can find the entry it needs to correct.

**The close-period tool lets a shadow close record its findings.** The MCP tool checked the close
gate before dispatching and refused on any blocker; a shadow close is refused only on the
structural gates, as the service already ran it.

**A QuickBooks disconnect leaves the company's grant when another graph uses it.** Intuit holds
one authorization per app and company, so disconnecting one graph, or deleting it, ended the
authorization of a second graph connected to the same company. This is the path a company takes
when it moves to a new graph.

## Reports from a company that is not on the platform

**An investor graph receives reports.** A graph with the `roboinvestor` extension alone carries
the reporting tables, so a report shared into it materializes and
`Portfolio → Position → Security → Entity → Report → Fact` resolves there. A report records how
it arrived (`origin`: authored, shared or uploaded), and the rules that protect a received report
follow that, not whether it has a source graph.

**`create-issuer` and `ingest-report`.** A fund adds a company as an issuer and loads its report
from a holon, a Tavi compiled model, or rows. Rows are assembled into a holon first, so every
report in the graph was loaded from a serialization that is stored and can be downloaded. The
report is checked before anything is written, and one that does not check is refused with the
numbers that disagree. A later ingest for the same company, period end and kind replaces the
earlier one.

**A statement sent as values is laid out from the library.** A caller sends the values of a
balance sheet or an income statement; each becomes a line under the nearest line above it that
also has a value, and every total is checked against the lines beneath it. A firm's own line is
given the line it adds into. A received primary statement keeps the library's structure, reads
back in the document's own wording, and a departure from the library's arrangement is recorded on
the response.

**Limits on what a report holds.** A report sent as rows takes at most 3,000 values and 750
concepts, and a Tavi model is held to the same counts. A graph keeps receiving reports past
fifty: the extension that holds them is no longer checked against the size caps of a single
authoring request. A value the report states twice for one concept and period loads once, the
more precise of the two.

**A ledger's fact grid answers for its own entities.** On a graph that keeps a ledger and has
received another company's report, `build-fact-grid` with no entity filter leaves out the
companies whose reports were received, so a sum over a concept is the group's own.

**A share carries a current holon, and any recipient can leave it.** A share takes a fresh holon
when the report's columns moved since the last stamp. A graph with `roboinvestor` alone can
remove a received report and refuse its sender.

**A value total over some positions says so.** The portfolio block and the holdings read gain
`marked_position_count` and `current_value_is_partial`. The total itself is unchanged.

## The SEC repository trial

**A first subscription to a shared repository starts its trial without a card.** A card added
before the trial ends keeps the plan; without one the trial ends with nothing charged and access
ends with a message that says so. Starting a trial needs a verified email. A trial checkout
records a card only when one was given, and Checkout offers no promotion code field.

**Checkout refuses a repository seat the user already holds.** `POST /v1/billing/checkout` answers
409 when the user's own subscription to the repository is in force, so a seat on a card-free
trial is changed from the subscriptions page, not bought a second time.

**A lapsed repository subscription says so over MCP**, with where to subscribe, in place of a
generic refusal.

## Ledger and reporting

**Aged receivables and payables on native books.** An invoice, bill or payment drafted on books
RoboLedger keeps, and posted by a close, now reaches `aged-balances`, the open-items reads and the
per-counterparty balances; before, it never aged. A document whose posted entry was since
reversed leaves them again, and a reversed payment no longer settles its invoice. **These change
the figures those reads return on native books.** Books QuickBooks keeps are unchanged.

**A closed-month remap may not move cash or equity,** and every mapping arc an account gains in
one update is judged against its closed months, not only the first.

**The legacy flow key takes the Style check,** and the equity statement names what it leaves out.

**Amounts in cents and share counts no longer stop at 32 bits.** GraphQL's `Int` failed the whole
read on a value past $21,474,836.47 in cents. Those fields cross as a `BigInt` scalar, still a
JSON number. A client that declares one of these fields' types in its own query variables names
`BigInt` from this release.

## MCP and operators

**The RoboLedger route exposes each operation as its own tool.** `/v1/mcp/roboledger` shows every
operation a model can call up front, with its own input schema, and serves the same tool set as
every tenant connection apart from what a chat client cannot use. The universal and per-graph
routes keep every tool they had and gain the new typed reads.

**The author operator updates only what its own request created.** A Console `/do` request that
asks to change an existing forecast, schedule or counterparty is refused with where to make the
edit. It can still create one and adjust it within the same request.

**An operator run keeps the prompt and tools its model was given,** stored once per graph by
hash, with the sampling settings on every model call and the code version on the run.

**The analyst recalls memories for a long question.**

## Email

**Transactional email is sent from the API,** from the request's background task, in one branded
layout. Verification, password reset, welcome, invitation, passkey and email-change messages
arrive in seconds; each took a Dagster run before. `send_email_job` stays as the retry lane.
Verifying an email clears the cached profile, so the app sees it at once.

## Bank feeds

**Mercury's intake follows the feed's own corrections.** An incremental sync looks back from the
earlier of the last successful sync and today, so a quiet feed loses nothing; a line Mercury
reverses, fails or cancels is removed when unposted and held as a reconciling item when posted;
and the two legs of a transfer pair within three days, closest date first. A re-consent is held
to the organization the connection was first made to. Mercury stays off in the hosted product.

## Security

- An OAuth refresh repeated within 60 seconds of its rotation gets a sibling pair, so connectors
  that share one account's stored token are no longer signed out together.
- An issued access token is an identity on its first call.
- Records read back from the shared cache are checked for integrity.
- The Graph API admits traffic from its client security group only.
- Indexing a document no longer holds the API's event loop.

## Infrastructure

- Migrations run on the orchestrator's boot: on the platform database, the operator run contexts
  and code version; on the extensions database, a report's `origin`, in every tenant.
- Stack updates ride the deploy for the VPC, API, worker, Dagster, bastion and graph stacks: the
  Graph API's client security group, the services that carry it, and the graph tier's ingress
  from it.
- A dedicated read login for staging scans.
- The test suite builds tenant schemas once per worker.
- The repository's Claude commands are skills.

A deployment on v1.23.0 restarts into this release with no manual step. The apps that read the
new `eventBlocks` argument and the `BigInt` fields (`@robosystems/client` 2.41.2 and later) deploy
after this release is live.
